case: ArmedSet, which declares no exclusive factory, is given one that IS a registered command.
why: The check must resolve names, not refuse change. A record acquiring an exclusive factory is an ordinary tightening -- it is the direction the contract wants to move -- and a control that refused it would make declaring a creation path more expensive than leaving it open, which is backwards. This also proves the ordinary branch of the resolution is live: the command registry is consulted, not just the three-path kernel literal.
